title: Canary rollout postmortem: automated safety gates, probe hysteresis, and rollback TTLs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During a recent canary rollout of model v2.3 we observed a progressive increase in bad response rates across a small percentage of traffic and an eventual failed auto-rollback because the safety gate hysteresis allowed transient noise to be treated as stable regressions. This ticket captures the postmortem actions and tracks engineering work to harden canary safety gates, add automated sanity-runbooks, and implement a configurable rollback TTL and probe smoothing to avoid flapping.

Goals: 
- Collect incident learnings and formalize them into a canary safety runbook.
- Implement probe hysteresis and exponential backoff to reduce false positives from transient spikes.
- Add a rollback TTL and a circuit-breaker to prevent repeated rollbacks within short windows.
- Create automated canary dashboards and alert thresholds tied to traffic-weighted metrics.
- Add an audit log and post-deploy checklist that must pass before canary promotes beyond 5% traffic.

Scope: runtime canary controller, Redwood Console rollout UI, alerting rules in PagerDuty/Dashboards, runbook docs, and a follow-up QA pass on dedicated capacity behavior.

Success criteria: 
- New runbook published to Confluence with a clear escalation path and playbook steps.
- Canary controller implements smoothing and rollback TTL (configurable per-release).
- Observability dashboards with synthetic probe traces and traffic-weighted SLOs available in staging and production.
- One simulated canary test with injected faults runs cleanly (no false rollback) before rollout to customers.

Notes: This is time-sensitive because the customer who triggered the incident is on a dedicated capacity contract and expects a write-up plus mitigations within 2 weeks.
comments: 2025-02-20 — Aisha Patel: Filed after incident INC-2025-112. Initial triage: regression signature was 0.8% bad_response_rate at 3% traffic increasing to 2.6% over 30 minutes. Canary controller rolled back once then failed to re-promote; logs show hysteresis window configured at 5 minutes which allowed noisy spike to be interpreted as sustained regression.

2025-02-21 — Marcelo Ruiz: Reproduced locally with traffic replay. Root cause appears to be twofold: (1) probe smoothing configured as simple moving average with short window; (2) rollback policy lacks TTL so subsequent canary promotions immediately retriggered the same checks. Drafting patch for smoothing and TTL config in canary controller.

2025-02-24 — SRE Review (Lindsey Wong): Recommended adding median-based probe plus percentile trimming to avoid outlier-driven signals. Also suggested a temporary alert to page on 1.5% sustained bad_response_rate over 20 minutes during canary windows.
2025-02-27 — Design (Hiro Tanaka): Console UX update: expose a 'safety profile' selector (conservative, balanced, aggressive) with defaults and per-release overrides. Planned mockups linked.

2025-03-02 — Marcelo Ruiz: Draft PR submitted implementing exponential smoothing (alpha configurable) and rollback_ttl_seconds with default 3600s. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4821

2025-03-04 — QA (Priya Desai): Ran canary simulation with injected 0.5% latency noise and 2x error spikes for 3 minutes — no false positive rollback after smoothing enabled; TTL prevented immediate re-rollouts. Pending integration tests in dedicated capacity environment.
decision_log: 2025-02-22: Agreed to implement exponential smoothing (configurable alpha) rather than longer simple moving average to keep responsiveness to real regressions.
2025-02-23: TTL for rollback set to default 1 hour (3600s) with per-project override up to 24h. This prevents thrashing on releases with transient infra noise.

2025-02-27: Add safety profiles to Console UI. Conservative profile uses 2x sensitivity threshold and 15-minute hysteresis; Balanced uses current defaults; Aggressive is for fast iteration only behind manual approval.
2025-03-01: Require a synthetic probe pass (end-to-end) with traffic replay for every canary before crossing 5% traffic in production for Dedicated customers.
next_steps: Merge PR #4821 and rollout to staging cluster behind feature flag (assigned Marcelo).
Add a temporary PagerDuty alert rule for sustained bad_response_rate during canary windows (assigned Lindsey).
Publish Canary Safety Runbook and link checklist to Console promotion flow (assigned Aisha).
Design finalize mockups and handoff to frontend for safety profile selector (assigned Hiro).
Schedule dedicated capacity integration test with customer-rep traffic replay (assigned Priya).
